items.summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
items.title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

items.summary: This paper develops the Phase Compatibility branch of Harmonic Physics: a framework for examining how physical participants enter constrained phase relations, produce collective outcomes, and form persistent higher-level organisations capable of further recursive participation. Building on established synchronization theory, phase locking, coupled-oscillator dynamics and phasor mathematics, the framework examines reinforcement, opposition, cancellation, reshaping and whole formation. It distinguishes mathematical admissibility, actual source occupancy, participant admission, active interaction, closure, continuing identity and observation. A compatibility basin is characterised through maintained relational organisation and persistence under declared conditions. Version 3.1 aligns the shared definitions with the current Foundations and Observer Theory papers, corrects the amplitude-weighted moment family, and clarifies the distinction between passive changes of representation and physical projection or coupling. It incorporates the completed mathematical nesting construction, which preserves a supplied quantum state’s amplitude and relative-phase information, together with Born probabilities under corresponding joint measurements. Phase Theory Equations is identified as the consolidated reference for the current mathematical expressions. The observation account separates source organisation, information encoded into light, receiver coupling, registration, retention and calibrated reconstruction. Within the proposed optical terminology, light performs the observer role through source–receiver coupling, while the receiver registers and retains a physical response. Minimal relational consciousness and awareness retain separate definitions. The paper integrates controlled models, molecular spectral studies, a superconducting-qubit analogue, simulated liquid-water reorganisation, quantum-state encoding and specified receiver models, preserving the scope and limitations of each result. It sets out the state spaces, conservation requirements, comparison models and prospective failure conditions required for physical applications. Universal participant-admission and whole-formation laws remain open research questions; this revision introduces no new experimental validation.
items.title: Phase Compatibility: Harmonic Combination, Selective Participation, Whole Formation, and Recursive Organisation

Its core three-coupling is Acupoint Microenvironments x Multimodal Metrology x Paired Control. The principal White Rainbow Epoch Hypothesis is deliberately vulnerable to refutation: analysts blinded to point identity must be able to reconstruct an independently calibrated advantage when equally hydrated measurement sites are exchanged under a concealed test condition. Skin water content, contact pressure, temperature, electrode polarization, ordinary neurovascular anatomy, skin pigmentation, photon pathlength and site-selection bias are treated as strong competing explanations, not minor caveats. The civilizational purpose follows a governing three-coupling: Continuity of Chinese Cultural Heritage x Exploration through Modern Science x Original Civilizational Interpretation of the White Rainbow Epoch. Classical acupuncture, Chinese medical philosophy, yin-yang, Five Phases and Daoist thought are welcomed as inherited cultural frameworks capable of generating questions. They are not relabelled novel SI-measurable energy fields or independently validated clinical mechanisms. Established physical laws and metrological statistics likewise remain inherited knowledge rather than purported discoveries by 33 x STARLI. Newly composed, falsifiable interdisciplinary proposals are marked White Rainbow Epoch Hypotheses. Cultural interpretation may remain meaningful even when a particular physical hypothesis fails. The book contains 30 mechanism-distinct golden mathematical plates, 82 scientific chapters and 410 individually paginated research investigations, 200 one-page Research Gates whose large deep-navy opening questions lead to discriminating experiments, and 33 scientifically distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. The plates include complex impedance, electrode polarization, pressure and hydration sensitivity, optical pathlength, chromophore inversion, heat transport, oxygen diffusion, spatial statistics, hierarchical and covariance-aware inference, multiplicity, null-equivalence and hard integrity vetoes. The Gates present concrete blinded challenges, resource-matched traditional metrology baselines, necessary calibration and acceptance margins, failure pathways and independent handoff requirements. Each Phoenix embryo has a different named instrument or provisional mechanism, adversarial test, rival explanation and honest metamorphosis path when rejected. The editorial DOI scope is intentionally limited to three author-associated STARLI mother research volumes: 10.5281/zenodo.23480803 (AI Microrobotic Sensing of Senescent-Cell Heterogeneity at the Limit), 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 (Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit), and 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 (Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit). Their chapter lineages offer methodological ancestry in measurement provenance, bias governance, independent requalification and sample-state preservation. They are not independent evidence that the proposed acupoint effect exists. The project does not exclude established scientific knowledge or ancient philosophy; it simply does not include other authors' DOI records in this particular bibliography.

items.summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.
items.title: Chinese and Mayan Dice: Circular Chains, Explicit Constructions, and Decision Theory

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. Circular pores can provide more uniform stress distribu

items.summary: Two datasets recording immigration detention oversight in the inspecting bodies' and ICE's own published language. The inspections dataset (207 rows) gives the most recent published inspection per facility from ICE Office of Detention Oversight reports in the ICE FOIA Library 2025–2026 listing window (179 facilities) plus the 28 facility-specific DHS Office of Inspector General detention inspection reports of fiscal years 2021–2026, with each report's published Facility Rating and deficient-standards count reproduced verbatim, never re-graded. The deaths dataset (84 rows) lists the deaths in ICE custody in ICE's Detainee Death Reporting tables for fiscal years 2021–2026, each with the ICE death report ICE itself published (name, age, country of citizenship, facility, date of death, and cause of death where the report states one). Sources: ICE FOIA Library, DHS Office of Inspector General, and ICE Detainee Death Reporting, retrieved October 23, 2026. Tool: https://inspections-ledger.straitresearch.org/. Direction and final calls by Athena Anthea; research judgment and technical execution shared with an AI assistant. Version 1.1 (October 24, 2026) adds: a published facility-name crosswalk (200 canonical facilities) with single-facility dossiers joining ODO, OIG, and deaths records per facility; an extraction naming the deficient standards behind the published counts for 52 of the 179 ODO inspection rows (validated by hand-checking 10 reports; coverage and per-row failure reasons stated, never guessed); and deaths tables showing cause stated (12) vs not stated (72) by fiscal year and facility.
items.title: Inspections & Deaths Ledger: detention facility inspection results and deaths in ICE custody from the official record — a Strait Research dataset

items.summary: HIGH-INTEGRITY CARGO TRANSPORT AND CONTROLLED RELEASE IN MICRO/NANOROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT English Introduction This high-density research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for high-integrity microrobotic cargo transport and controlled release. Arrival is explicitly separated from delivery: one identified cargo lineage must remain bound through transport, stay below registered shear thermal and chemical exposure limits, avoid premature leakage and cross-contamination, release inside the authorized spatial and temporal window, preserve a cargo-specific functional endpoint, and leave a closed record of residual material and carrier recovery. Thirty physicalized derivations connect directly to 82 chapters, 410 single-page research studies, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. When unknown shear pulses, constrictions, sham triggers, second cargo lots, and carrier aging are introduced blindly, the system must lower both premature leakage and nonrelease rather than exchange one failure for the other. Missing mass, destructive triggering, target expansion, and deleted failed cargo reject the claim.

items.summary: we hereby submit our manuscript entitled “Query-Defined Submodels: Publishing Topological Graph Analyses to the Asset Administration Shell” for consideration for publication as an Article in the Industrial Informatics and Digital Twin section of Machines (MDPI).The manuscript proposes a unidirectional pipeline that combines graph-based analysis with standardized information exchange through the Asset Administration Shell (AAS). It addresses a specific limitation of AAS-QL regarding traversal through RelationshipElement endpoints, performs the required topological analysis in a property-graph environment, and exports the selected and potentially derived result as a standards-conformant AAS Submodel. The approach is formalized mathematically by representing the analysis as a mapping from a labelled property graph to a result graph and the export as a second mapping fSrom that result into an AAS Submodel. This makes explicit that the exported extent is query-defined. The proposed architecture is further evaluated analytically with respect to communication and maintenance costs under different production-system configurations.

items.summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-24:   The black hole. A black hole is understood as the construction of mass from the large end: particles build mass from the small end, the black hole from the large one. Perception has a limit of tempo: a process whose tempo is below our smallest does not change for us, so the centre is inaccessible, and for us it is space possessing mass and rotation. The horizon is the transition from space into mass; it grows with mass and is not related to the core. The black hole processes volumetric particles into a plane, and the tension of space, when the sizes of galaxies change, again gives birth to particle–antiparticle pairs: the cycle is closed. Only black holes that are analogues of elementary particles are considered. G and α. Both constants have received a geometric reading. Gravity is the work of space in a cross-section, charge is the same work over a closed surface; the surface of a sphere is four times its cross-section, hence the four. Charge is the work of one unpaired half-wave, that is, of one step of the microworld k: 1/α = 4k. G is gravity from the large end: the whole linear path up to the transition and the step linking it with the small end, G = 1/(c·c^(1/5)), without the four. The link of the two constants is G = 4α/((2π)^(1/5)·c). In neutral particles the same transition from flat to volume goes through rotation (support: the magnetic moment of the neutron). The residuals of 0.22 % in α and 0.8 % in G are not yet explained.       Работа строит основу физики из одного допущения: всё — процесс, а процесс — идеальный синус; его центр, баланс, — наблюдатель. Между уровнями проходит только квадрат — интенсивност

items.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

items.summary: IrrMapper is a Random Forest classification of Landsat imagery that maps irrigated agriculture each year at 30 m across Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. This deposit is the GeoTIFF release of version 1.2, the product served in the Google Earth Engine public data catalog as UMT/Climate/IrrMapper_RF/v1_2. One zip per state holds one cloud-optimized GeoTIFF per year (450 files; California begins in 1986), the state boundary polygon used for clipping, and grids.json describing every state's raster grid. Values: 1 irrigated, 0 not irrigated, 255 nodata. All files are in EPSG:5070 (NAD83 / Conus Albers) at 30 m on one shared pixel lattice, so all years of a state stack without resampling and neighboring states align pixel for pixel. SHA256 checksums are provided for every GeoTIFF and archive. See README.md for the format, grid definition, provenance and known limitations.

items.summary: The attribution of downwind rainfall changes to irrigation expansion remains contested because irrigation modifies both surface moisture and boundary-layer thermodynamics, and because satellite retrievals of convective initiation are sparse and noisy. The framework combines a potential-outcomes formulation with a honest random-forest splitting rule that permits effect modification by land-surface and atmospheric covariates. A formal result establishes that the forest estimator is consistent for the conditional average treatment effect when the propensity score is known and the retrieval error is classical, and a sensitivity bound quantifies bias under differential misclassification. The framework is then applied in a methodological evaluation using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations), where the mean temperature was 26.414 °C and the warming trend was 0.1553 °C per decade. The evaluation clarifies the conditions under which downwind rainfall attribution is credible and identifies the retrieval-error regimes in which causal-forest estimates should be preferred to regression-adjustment alternatives.
tags: causal forest; irrigation expansion; convective initiation; satellite retrievals; downwind rainfall;
items.title: Causal forest estimation of irrigation-expansion feedbacks on convective initiation from paired satellite retrievals: a climate-analytics evaluation of downwind rainfall attribution

items.summary: After more than a decade of development, high-resolution spectroscopy plays a central role in the atmospheric characterization of exoplanets, offering insights into planetary chemical composition, thermal structure, and atmospheric dynamics. Among the most intriguing targets for atmospheric characterization are Ultra-Hot Jupiters (UHJs), which, due to their extreme temperatures and intense stellar irradiation, serve as unique laboratories for studying planetary atmospheres under extreme conditions. In this talk, I will discuss what we can learn and what challenges we must confront when interpreting high-resolution observations of UHJs, using KELT-9b (equilibrium temperature ~4000 K) as a benchmark case. Based on transmission and emission observations obtained with the near-infrared spectrograph GIANO-B at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG), I explore how different modeling assumptions impact the detectability and interpretation of atmospheric signals. In particular, the extreme irradiation conditions of these planets may give rise to departures from local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), making non-LTE effects potentially non-negligible. At the same time, the strong day–night temperature contrasts and asymmetric terminator regions expected in UHJs challenge the applicability of 1D atmospheric models, which may lead to biased or incomplete interpretations of the observed signals.   These effects can have important consequences for the inferred atmospheric abundances and bias the interpretation of key quantities such as the C/O and R/H ratios, which are used to constrain planetary formation and evolutionary scenarios. Addressing these challenges is therefore crucial to robustly link high-resolution observations of UHJs to their origins.
items.title: INTERPRETING EXTREME ATMOSPHERES: Lessons from High-Resolution spectroscopy of an Ultra-Hot Jupiter

items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.
tags: physics-informed neural networks; rainfall extremes; tail-index distortion; dam safety; radiosonde i
items.title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics

items.summary: Carbon-credit methodologies for mangrove restoration typically assume that credited carbon storage persists for a fixed horizon, yet staggered enrollment and unobserved baseline dynamics make permanence risk difficult to identify from satellite time series alone. The framework combines a potential-outcomes model for staggered adoption with a hidden-Markov representation of unobserved baseline loss, and derives bounds on the bias of the conventional permanence deduction. Analysis of the identification conditions shows that the standard deduction is unbiased only when baseline loss is independent of enrollment timing, an assumption that fails whenever enrollment is targeted at high-threat sites. The derived bounds imply that permanence-risk overstatement is increasing in the correlation between enrollment timing and baseline threat, and that the sign of the bias can be recovered from observable enrollment-date and land-cover-covariate patterns. The contribution is a diagnostic that credit issuers can apply to existing registries without new field data, together with a formal statement of the conditions under which the conventional deduction is defensible.
tags: mangrove restoration; carbon credits; additionality; permanence risk; causal inference; Landsat time
items.title: Causal inference on mangrove-restoration carbon-credit additionality from Landsat time series under staggered enrollment: an artificial intelligence evaluation of permanence-risk overstatement

items.summary: Minimal unbiased compositional change generates a source operation algebra with compact internal and Lorentzian event realizations. On the least-dimensional compact connected faithful irreducible orthogonal carrier, independent composition and square-root scaling with unit covariance fix the centred Gaussian law. Its ladder and coherent comparisons generate the round SU(2) S U ( 2 ) process spectrum; complete centre-invariant observations give RP3 R P 3 . Within complete continuations preserving adjoints, exchange structures, source phase and reversal, three theorems characterize relative frames, least faithful matter and the elementary scalar connector. The faithfully acting group is (SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1))/Z6 ( S U ( 3 ) × S U ( 2 ) × U ( 1 )) / Z 6 acting on a sixteen-dimensional full matter module with a fifteen-dimensional charged quotient. The elementary connector has one complex scalar doublet coordinate. The colour connection supplies a collective intensity, Casimir feedback and the long-root drive. The complete spectral response has a unique positive equilibrium at the source-calibrated IR radius Lsrc=2π>Lc=π L src = 2 π > L c = π . Its normalized radial curvature and common-frame coexact response form the generated Yang-Mills mass operator. Its equilibrium Gaussian response completion has a unique vacuum and an attained positive gap. The original connection polynomials embed with their source state and ordinary products intact, and the representation intertwines the equilibrium update. Explicit Hermite weights describe their curvature correlations, and the joint curvature susceptibility detects the collective radial response. A source phase clock calibrates timelike translation on the event carrier. Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction gives free local fields. At gauge-compatible finite internal resolution, causal perturbation theory realizes the native vertices as a local net. Its physical net is the quantum BRST cohomology, with anomaly cancellation ensuring the Ward identities at every order in the renormalizable gauge-matter realization. In the quadratic realization, colour intensity has a radial pole and explicit multiparticle continua.

items.summary: Background: Vitamin D, vitamin B12 and thyroid results are often available at a first headache visit, but their relation to later acute treatment is unclear, and testing is selective. We estimated whether 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], vitamin B12, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (T4) recorded at the first headache visit were associated with acute analgesic prescribing from that day onward. Methods: Retrospective electronic health record cohort of 10,898 adults with a new headache code (G43, G44, R51) at a secondary-care neurology clinic in Türkiye, 2023–2024, with linked laboratory results. As results were carried forward, the exposure was the most recent value recorded at the first visit. The outcome was ≥2 acute analgesic prescription items. Odds ratios (OR) per standard deviation (SD) were estimated with inverse probability-of-measurement weighting, with complete-case and imputed analyses; the equivalence margin was 0.80–1.25. Results: Values were recorded for 47.7% (25(OH)D) to 77.3% (TSH). Weighted ORs per SD were 1.04 (0.95–1.14) for 25(OH)D, 1.01 (0.94–1.08) for vitamin B12, 0.96 (0.90–1.02) for TSH and 0.94 (0.88–1.01) for free T4; all 95% intervals included 1 (false discovery rate–adjusted q ≥ 0.34), and estimates were similar for a migraine index code. All four 90% intervals lay within 0.80–1.25, although equivalence was not claimed for 25(OH)D. Conclusion: In the primary weighted analysis, these markers were not associated with acute analgesic prescribing, so first-visit values may not help anticipate acute treatment needs. Recorded laboratory fields need timing and selection checks before use as exposures. Preprint, not peer reviewed. Online Resource 1 (supplementary methods and tables) is included as a separate file.
items.title: Vitamin D, vitamin B12 and thyroid function recorded at the first headache-coded visit and later acute analgesic prescribing: a routine-records cohort study
